def find_subsets(remaining, k):
    if k == 1:
        return [list(remaining)]
    remaining = sorted(remaining)
    first = remaining[0]
    rest = remaining[1:]
    # find subsets containing first that sum to target

def girth(edges, n):
    from collections import defaultdict, deque
    adj = defaultdict(set)
    for u,v in edges:
        adj[u].add(v); adj[v].add(u)
    g = float('inf')
    for src in range(n):
        dist = {src: 0}
        parent = {src: -1}
        q = deque([src])
        while q:
            u = q.popleft()
            for v in adj[u]:
                if v not in dist:
                    dist[v] = dist[u]+1
                    parent[v] = u
                    q.append(v)
                elif parent[u] != v:
                    # found cycle
                    cl = dist[u] + dist[v] + 1
                    if cl < g: g = cl
    return g

        added = False
        random.shuffle(candidates)
        new_cands = []
        for u,v in candidates:

            # Check girth: BFS
            dist = {u:0}
            q = [u]
            ok = True
            for d in range(7):
                nq = []

    return edges

def encode(num_edges):
    solver = Glucose3()
    # For girth >= 6, forbid all cycles of length 3, 4, 5.
    from itertools import combinations
    # Triangles: for each triple, not all three edges
    for a,b,c in combinations(range(n),3):
        e1 = var_of[(a,b)]; e2 = var_of[(a,c)]; e3 = var_of[(b,c)]
        solver.add_clause([-e1,-e2,-e3])
    # 4-cycles: for each set of 4 vertices, forbid any 4-cycle
    for quad in combinations(range(n),4):
        a,b,c,d = quad
        # three perfect matchings form 4-cycles: (ab,cd)+(ac,bd), etc.
        # cycle a-b-c-d-a uses edges ab,bc,cd,da
        for perm in [(a,b,c,d),(a,b,d,c),(a,c,b,d)]:
            w,x,y,z = perm
            e1 = var_of[(min(w,x),max(w,x))]
            e2 = var_of[(min(x,y),max(x,y))]
            e3 = var_of[(min(y,z),max(y,z))]
            e4 = var_of[(min(z,w),max(z,w))]
            solver.add_clause([-e1,-e2,-e3,-e4])
    # 5-cycles
    for quint in combinations(range(n),5):
        from itertools import permutations
        seen = set()
        for perm in permutations(quint):

            # canonical
            a = min(range(5), key=lambda i: perm[i])
            rot = perm[a:]+perm[:a]
            if rot[1] > rot[-1]:

            if rot in seen: continue
            seen.add(rot)
            edges_in_cycle = []
            for i in range(5):
                u,v = rot[i], rot[(i+1)%5]
                edges_in_cycle.append(var_of[(min(u,v),max(u,v))])
            solver.add_clause([-e for e in edges_in_cycle])

    lits = list(var_of.values())
    cnf = CardEnc.atleast(lits=lits, bound=num_edges, top_id=len(pairs), encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
    for cl in cnf.clauses:

    return solver

from pysat.card import CardEnc, EncType
from pysat.formula import IDPool

G = 30  # golfers
W = 8   # weeks
K = 10  # groups per week
S = 3   # group size

    return vpool.id(('x', w, p, g))
def m(w, p, q):  # p<q, same group in week w
    return vpool.id(('m', w, p, q))

clauses = []

        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.pairwise)
        clauses.extend(cnf.clauses)

# Each group has exactly S players

    for g in range(K):
        lits = [x(w,p,g) for p in range(G)]
        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=S, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
        clauses.extend(cnf.clauses)

# Symmetry: week 0 fixed: players 3g, 3g+1, 3g+2 in group g

        clauses.append([x(0, 3*g+i, g)])

# Alternative: for each pair p<q and week w, at most one g has both.
# And: sum over w of "same in week w" <= 1.

# Define y(w,p,q,g) = x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g). For p<q.
# m(w,p,q) = OR_g y(w,p,q,g)
# Then sum_w m(w,p,q) <= 1.

# Simpler encoding: for each pair p<q and each week w, define same via:
# same(w,p,q) <- x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g)  for each g
# For upper bound use: sum_w sum_g (x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g)) <= 1
# But AND isn't directly a literal. Introduce aux z(w,p,q,g).

# Actually easier: for each pair p<q, for each week w: at most one common group.
# And forbid pair meeting more than once. 
# Introduce meet(w,p,q): if both x(w,p,g) and x(w,q,g), then meet(w,p,q).
# Add: x(w,p,g) AND x(w,q,g) -> meet(w,p,q)
# Then sum_w meet(w,p,q) <= 1.

for p in range(G):

        meets = []

            meets.append(mv)
            for g in range(K):

                clauses.append([-x(w,p,g), -x(w,q,g), mv])
        cnf = CardEnc.atmost(lits=meets, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)

print("clauses:", len(clauses), "vars:", vpool.top)

from pysat.solvers import Glucose4
from pysat.card import CardEnc, EncType
from pysat.formula import IDPool

G = 50  # golfers
S = 5   # group size
K = 10  # groups
W = 6   # weeks

vpool = IDPool()
# x[w][g][p] = 1 if golfer p in group g in week w
def x(w,g,p):
    return vpool.id(('x',w,g,p))

# y[w][p][q] = 1 if golfers p<q together in week w
def y(w,p,q):
    return vpool.id(('y',w,p,q))

solver = Glucose4()

# Each golfer in exactly one group per week
for w in range(W):
    for p in range(G):
        lits = [x(w,g,p) for g in range(K)]
        # exactly one
        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.pairwise)
        for cl in cnf.clauses:
            solver.add_clause(cl)

# Each group has exactly S golfers per week
for w in range(W):
    for g in range(K):
        lits = [x(w,g,p) for p in range(G)]
        cnf = CardEnc.equals(lits=lits, bound=S, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
        for cl in cnf.clauses:
            solver.add_clause(cl)

# y[w,p,q] <=> exists g with x(w,g,p) and x(w,g,q)
# We need: if y=1 then sum over g of (x(w,g,p) AND x(w,g,q)) >= 1
# Simpler: define z(w,g,p,q) = x(w,g,p) AND x(w,g,q). Use y=OR of z.
# Then constraint sum_w y[w,p,q] <= 1.
# But we can avoid y by: for each pair (p,q), sum over w,g of z(w,g,p,q) <= 1.
# z(w,g,p,q) <=> x(w,g,p) & x(w,g,q). z -> x(w,g,p), z -> x(w,g,q), x&x -> z.
# Actually we just need sum_{w,g} (x(w,g,p)*x(w,g,q)) <= 1 which means pair together at most once.

# Using auxiliary z variables:
def z(w,g,p,q):
    return vpool.id(('z',w,g,p,q))

for p in range(G):
    for q in range(p+1,G):
        zlits = []
        for w in range(W):
            for g in range(K):
                zv = z(w,g,p,q)
                # z -> xp
                solver.add_clause([-zv, x(w,g,p)])
                solver.add_clause([-zv, x(w,g,q)])

                solver.add_clause([-x(w,g,p), -x(w,g,q), zv])

        cnf = CardEnc.atmost(lits=zlits, bound=1, vpool=vpool, encoding=EncType.seqcounter)
